section_summary.extract_value: This INTRODUCTION reviews literature linking early affiliative experiences and social safeness to psychological wellbeing and eating psychopathology, and defines body appreciation as a protective, compassionate attitude toward one's body. It states the current study aims to test an integrative model where recall of early warmth influences eating psychopathology via social safeness and body appreciation; no study labels (e.g., 'Study 1') or sample/method details are provided in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted summary sentences drawn from the INTRODUCTION: 'The current study aimed to test an integrative model that explores the impact of the recall of early memories of warmth and safeness on eating psychopathology, and whether social safeness and body appreciation significantly act on this association.' and multiple earlier sentences describing constructs (e.g., 'Body appreciation, defined as a positive, accepting and respecting attitude towards body image...').
